source_records.title: CaTSCAN: Calculating Typed Subgraph Counts Analytically for Networks
source_records.abstract: Large graphs can be considered to be made of small subgraphs, called graphlets , that make up its fundamental building blocks. Therefore, counting graphlet frequencies is valuable for understanding structural characteristics and function of a given graph. In this paper, we propose an efficient algorithm CaTSCAN for counting the exact frequencies of typed graphlets of size up to 5 nodes in heterogeneous information networks, where the nodes of the graph (and graphlets) are assigned different types. Existing work has only addressed simpler problems, either focused on counting untyped graphlets of sizes up to 5 nodes, or in the case of typed graphlets, only considered counting graphlets with 3 and 4 nodes. CaTSCAN avoids excessive enumeration of individual graphlet instances by deriving the counts of larger graphlets from smaller ones with non-trivial and highly efficient combinatorics, while preserving type information. In an experimental evaluation, we show that CaTSCAN outperforms existing typed graphlet solutions on real-world datasets by up to 4 orders of magnitude for counting 3- and 4-node graphlets, and counts 5-node graphlets in less time than existing solutions count 3- and 4-node graphlets. CaTSCAN can even out-speed some untyped baselines on larger graphs.

source_records.title: Temporal Graph Classification Based on Fast and Exact Transitive Reduction Strategy
source_records.abstract: Temporal graphs are a variety of structured data that have been particularly studied recently. In this paper, we focus on classification of temporal graphs. Previous works have shown that such task can be tackled by first transforming temporal graphs to static ones using ad-hoc algorithms, before the classification step. However, resulting static graphs might be of huge size. Transitive reduction can be used to reduce the size and redundancy of such graphs, but with a high complexity time. In this paper, we propose a fully dynamic algorithm that transforms temporal graphs into static ones while applying exact transitive reduction at the same time. This algorithm has a much reduced complexity than doing both steps separately, while producing exactly the same output graphs. We show in the experimental section that similar accuracy is achieved for a lower computational time.

source_records.title: A Multi-heuristic Approach to Workload Placement in Virtualisation Environments
source_records.abstract: Dynamic resource allocation represents one of the core benefits of server virtualisation. Within a cloud computing context, a user issues an infrastructure request, which is satisfied by spawning one or several virtual machines (VMs). We argue that tearing down VMs once the initial request completes can prove sub-optimal. Indeed, this implies that for every new infrastructure request, the VM creation procedure is applied and, therefore, incurs the VM creation overhead. In this reseach, we consider workload placement as the first response to an infrastructure request, followed by a VM placement when no running VM has the capacity to execute the workload. Our solution proposes a multi-heuristic approach to workload placement in VMs. First, we employ a compound scoring function in the vector bin packing (VBP) algorithm to optimally assign workloads to running VMs. Next, the remaining workloads are placed on available VMs using a beam search (BS)-flavoured ant colony optimisation (ACO). We present an empirical evaluation with varied configurations to demonstrate that coupling VBP and ACO enhances the placement quality.

source_records.title: TimeAgent: From Matches to Memories—Timeline Summarization for Sports Analytics
source_records.abstract: Timeline summarization aims to condense evolving information across multiple documents into coherent chronological narratives. In the sports domain, this task is particularly challenging due to the volume of news and the need to focus on user-preferred attributes such as specific players or teams. While prior work has explored generic timeline summarization, datasets supporting attribute-aware timeline summarization in sports remain limited. To address this, we introduce MulSports , a dataset designed to facilitate research on attribute-conditioned timeline summarization for sports news. MulSports comprises 2,000 news articles spanning football, cricket, kabaddi, hockey, and volleyball, paired with extracted player and team attributes and human-written timeline summaries. Each instance associates temporally ordered articles with a target attribute, enabling evaluation of both attribute focus and temporal coherence. To illustrate the utility of MulSports , we present an empirical analysis using a simple multi-modular pipeline that integrates temporal retrieval with large language models. Experimental results show that fine-tuned models outperform prompt-based baselines. MulSports provides a foundation for studying personalized and temporally grounded summarization in sports. The code, datasets, and Appendix material are made available through an anonymous GitHub repository ( https://anonymous.4open.science/r/TimeAgent-277B/ ).

source_records.title: Part-GNN: A Partitioning-Based Graph Neural Network for Efficient Memory Large Scale Data Classification
source_records.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are a class of deep learning models that have demonstrated significant potential in various classification tasks, including image recognition and the prediction of labels for nodes and edges. Unlike traditional neural networks that operate on Euclidean data such as images or sequences, GNNs are specifically designed to handle non-Euclidean data, i.e. data represented as graphs, where relationships between entities are irregular and complex. These graphs may include rich node and edge attributes, making GNNs particularly suitable for domains such as social networks, molecular structures, and recommendation systems. Several GNN variants have been developed, including GCN, Cluster-GCN, GraphSAGE, and FastGCN. Despite their advantages, GNNs often require substantial memory, primarily due to the large adjacency matrices involved, which become computationally expensive for large-scale graphs. They also tend to have long training times. In this work, we propose a novel graph partitioning technique aimed at reducing the effective size of the graph while maintaining a high predictive F1-score. Furthermore, we integrate this partitioning approach with layer-wise training to enhance computational efficiency.

source_records.title: Design of a Query Expression for Multi-Dimensional Graph Warehousing
source_records.abstract: This study presents an extension of the conventional data warehouse query paradigm by introducing Multi-dimensional Graph eXpression (MGX), a multidimensional query framework designed to support Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) over graph-based business intelligence data. MGX extends the traditional Multi-Dimensional eXpression (MDX) syntax used in relational data warehouses by incorporating SQL-style analytical constructs, including GROUP BY, HAVING, and ORDER BY, thereby improving the expressive capability and flexibility of multidimensional analysis over graph warehouses. By bridging relational data warehousing technologies with graph-based analytical environments, the proposed framework addresses key limitations of traditional MDX in supporting graph-oriented analytics. It enables more effective exploration of semantically rich and socially connected knowledge embedded in networked datasets. Overall, MGX provides a practical methodological foundation for advancing graph warehousing and supporting next-generation network-centric business intelligence applications.

source_records.title: MambaDDI: A Hybrid State Space Framework for Multiclass Drug–Drug Interaction Prediction
source_records.abstract: Drug-Drug Interactions (DDIs) often cause significant adverse events, making early identification crucial, especially with rising polypharmacy. While most methods focus on binary prediction, multiclass DDI prediction is more advantageous as it identifies specific interaction types. However, this is challenging due to class imbalance, with many rare interaction types compared to dominant ones. We propose a multiclass DDI prediction framework comprising three components: Stage 1 involves feature extraction, where the molecular structures of two drugs are modeled as graphs using a graph attention network (GAT) as an encoder, then combined with Drug Repurposing Knowledge Graph (DRKG) embeddings to produce enhanced drug features. Stage 2 involves expert modelling, where the paired drug representations are processed by two Mamba State Space Model (SSM)- based experts: a standard Mamba expert and a class-reweighted Mamba expert, which efficiently capture sequential dependencies and interaction patterns between the drug representations. Stage 3 involves gated fusion, where a confidence-based gating strategy integrates the two experts to generate final predictions. The performance on DrugBank and DDIMDL benchmark datasets achieved macro F1 scores of 90.68% and 83.99%, demonstrating our framework’s effectiveness in multiclass DDI prediction. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/devalab/MambaDDI .

source_records.title: A Saliency-Driven Graph-Based Metric for fMRI-Based Visual Brain Decoding Evaluation
source_records.abstract: Recent progress in fMRI-based visual brain decoding has enabled the reconstruction of neural visual signals as high-quality images using diffusion-based generative models. However, evaluating the semantic fidelity of these reconstructions remains challenging. Existing metrics, primarily based on pixel-level similarity or global embeddings, fail to capture the saliency-driven, structural, and relational aspects central to human scene understanding. We propose a saliency-aware, graph-based similarity metric, SSG, that compares stimuli and reconstructions through compact semantic scene graphs centered on the most salient objects and their relationships. By integrating visual saliency, language-guided scene understanding, and instance-level grounding, our method produces weighted graph representations that emphasize meaningful content while suppressing background clutter. Reconstruction quality is assessed via saliency-weighted object and relation conformity, yielding an interpretable structural score aligned with human perceptual judgment. Experiments show that the proposed metric provides a more informative evaluation of visual brain reconstructions than existing alternatives and offers diagnostic insights that can guide reconstruction refinement.
